  act: report_problem(note?, record?)  [sensitive, settles later]
       Send one of this machine's problem records - a crash or failure this desktop wrote down, listed under `problems` in describe - to the project's report intake, with a note. Graded sensitive because the record leaves the machine. It carries no name, hostname or address; the bytes sent are exactly the record as the file holds it, which is what the Report a problem screen shows. The answer says where it landed.
         note?: string — What was happening, in your words. Optional.
         record?: string — The record's file name from `problems`, e.g. 1790120000-yantrik-studio.json. Left out means the newest.

  act: request_approval(action, app, grade, args_json?, purpose?, requester?)  [safe, settles on return]
       Ask the person at this machine to allow one action, once. Puts a card on their screen showing who is asking, what the action does, and every argument. Answer is `{request_id, status: "pending"}`; poll approval_status until it is granted or denied, then consume_approval before running the action. Asking is not being allowed: only a person pressing Allow creates a grant, and nothing on this surface can create one.
         action: string — The action's exact name, e.g. delete_event
         app: string — The app the action belongs to, e.g. calendar
         grade: string — The action's permission grade as os_describe reports it: safe, standard, sensitive or dangerous
         args_json?: object — The exact arguments, as a JSON object. The grant is bound to these — a different value later is a different action and will be refused
         purpose?: string — The action's own published description, so the card says what it does in the app's words
         requester?: string — What to call you on the card, e.g. hermes. It is shown as `says the caller`: nothing checks it, and it grants nothing. Beside it the card shows the program this machine worked out for itself from the socket, which is not taken from here
  act: approval_status(request_id)  [safe, settles on return]
       Where one approval request stands: pending, granted, denied, expired or consumed. `denied` is an answer, not a failure — do not ask again unless the person brings it up. `expired` means nobody answered in time.
         request_id: string — The id request_approval answered with
  act: consume_approval(action, app, request_id, args_json?)  [safe, settles on return]
       Spend a grant. Succeeds exactly once, and only if the person granted this request and the app, action and arguments are byte-for-byte what they were shown (key order aside). Anything else is refused, and the refusal says which part differed. Call it immediately before the action, and run the action only if it succeeded.
         action: string
         app: string
         request_id: string
         args_json?: object — The same JSON object the request carried
  act: record_unasked_action(action, app, grade, args_json?, mode?, outcome?, requester?)  [safe, settles on return]
       Write down one action that ran WITHOUT the person being asked — because the desktop is in auto or bypass mode, or because a session rule covers it. Call it straight after the action, with what actually happened. It records; it cannot authorise anything, and not calling it does not stop anything running. The person reads these in the mode menu and in ~/.local/share/yantrik/mind-audit.jsonl.
         action: string
         app: string
         grade: string — The action's grade, as os_describe reports it
         args_json?: object — The exact arguments it ran with, as a JSON object
         mode?: string — The mode it ran under: auto, bypass, or rule
         outcome?: string — What happened: ok, failed, or a short phrase
         requester?: string — What to call yourself in the record. Self-declared; the log also keeps what this machine established from the socket, separately
  act: close_mind_menu()  [safe, settles on return]
       Put away the mode menu — the one `show_mind_audit` opens over the mode chip, with the record of unasked actions in it. It changes nothing: the mode, its rules and the record stay as they are. `describe shell` says whether it is open under `mind_menu`.

  act: run_recipe(recipe, inputs?)  [sensitive, settles later]
       Start a recipe with its inputs: a built-in one by its name or id, or one a mind made. A formation — Council, Red team, Build, Writers' room; `describe shell` → `recipes` → `formations` lists each with its `inputs` — hands work to roles from the agent catalog: each works in its own pane on the Agents screen, its row saying which recipe it works for, and the recipe's stages light on the Recipes screen as they answer; its result comes as the recipe's completion. Answers with the run's id; `describe shell` → `recipes` shows how it goes, and `cancel_recipe` stops it and lets its agents go. An agent another agent or a recipe started cannot start a formation.
         recipe: string — The recipe's id from `describe shell` → `recipes`, or its name (Council, Build …)
         inputs?: object — Its inputs as a JSON object: {"question": "…"} for the Council, and a seat to change, e.g. "seat_2": "reviewer". `describe shell` → `recipes` → `formations` lists what each takes
  act: answer_recipe(recipe, text)  [standard, settles later]

         recipe: string — The recipe's id from `describe shell` → `recipes`, or its name
         text: string — The answer: one of the choices, or your own words
  act: pause_recipe(recipe)  [standard, settles later]

  act: resume_recipe(recipe)  [standard, settles later]
       Let a paused recipe go on — running, or waiting again on what it was waiting for

  act: cancel_recipe(recipe)  [standard, settles later]
       Stop a running, waiting or paused recipe for good. It cannot be resumed

  act: new_agent(mind, task)  [sensitive, settles on return]
       Start another agent — a new conversation with a mind — and give it a task. It works on its own, in its own pane on the Agents screen, and its row says you started it. Answers at once with its id; `read_agent` shows how it is going, `send_to_agent` says more, `stop_agent` stops it. It starts with nothing of yours: no grants, and anything it needs allowed is asked for again, in its own pane. An agent another agent started cannot start agents; one agent holds at most 3 running at once, and the desktop caps how many run in all. You are the agent named by the agent token your call carries beside `args` (YANTRIK_AGENT_TOKEN in yos's environment) — never an argument; with no token, the call is the person's.
         mind: string — Which mind: an attached one's id as `describe shell` lists under `minds` (pi, deepseek)
         task: string — What it is to do: its first prompt, in full
  act: send_to_agent(agent, text)  [standard, settles on return]
       Say more to an agent you started — its next prompt. Answers once it is sent; `read_agent` shows the answer as it comes. One turn at a time: an agent still on its last turn is not sent another. You are the agent named by the agent token your call carries beside `args` (YANTRIK_AGENT_TOKEN in yos's environment) — never an argument; with no token, the call is the person's.
         agent: string — The agent, as new_agent answered: `<mind>:<conversation>`
         text: string — What to say to it
  act: stop_agent(agent)  [standard, settles on return]
       Stop an agent you started: its turn is ended, every command it is running is killed (the whole process group), any approval it is waiting on is withdrawn, and the agents it started stop with it. Its pane stays readable. You are the agent named by the agent token your call carries beside `args` (YANTRIK_AGENT_TOKEN in yos's environment) — never an argument; with no token, the call is the person's.
         agent: string — The agent, as new_agent answered: `<mind>:<conversation>`
  act: read_agent(agent, last?)  [safe, settles on return]
       Read an agent's recent turns as text: what it was asked, what it said, each call it made with how it went and the end of its output, and what the person was asked for it. You may read yourself and the agents you started. You are the agent named by the agent token your call carries beside `args` (YANTRIK_AGENT_TOKEN in yos's environment) — never an argument; with no token, the call is the person's.
         agent: string — The agent, as new_agent answered: `<mind>:<conversation>`
         last?: integer — How many of its latest turns. Default 3, at most 20
  act: hand_off(role, task, context?, wait_seconds?)  [sensitive, settles on return]
       Hand a piece of work to a role from the agent catalog — Researcher, Planner, Coder, Reviewer, Red team, Writer, Chair, Scribe, or the person's own; `describe shell` lists them under `catalog` with what each is for, what it may touch and whether a mind it runs on is attached. It starts that role's agent on its first attached mind, in its own pane, with the role's standing instructions, your task and your context as its first prompt. It can act only within the role's reach: anything else it tries is refused. Without `wait_seconds` it answers at once with the agent's id; with it, it waits up to that long for the role's answer and hands it back. It starts with nothing of yours: no grants. An agent another agent started cannot hand off; one agent holds at most 3 running at once, and the desktop caps how many run in all. You are the agent named by the agent token your call carries beside `args` (YANTRIK_AGENT_TOKEN in yos's environment) — never an argument; with no token, the call is the person's.
         role: string — The role: its id as `describe shell` lists under `catalog` (reviewer, coder, red-team …), or its name
         task: string — What it is to do, in full: its first prompt, after the role's own instructions
         context?: string — What it should read first — the change to review, the answers to weigh. At most 32 KiB
         wait_seconds?: number — Seconds to wait for its answer. Left out, the answer is its id at once. At most 600
